title: Is my shop as busy as my graph says? Node.js cluster metrics, counted two ways
description: otel-cluster-metrics against the stock exporter, same app, same traffic.

options.content:
## Is my shop as busy as my graph says?
This synthetic shop runs twice. Both clusters have four workers and get the same request attempts. In the request-rate panel, **blue** merges worker metrics with [otel-cluster-metrics](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@adityareddy-dev/otel-cluster-metrics). **Orange** scrapes one stock exporter on a shared port. **Green** counts HTTP responses that the load generator receives from the merged shop, including 500s. Every four minutes a worker is replaced.

A hard kill can lose increments since the last worker snapshot, normally at most 10 seconds. The merged count is telemetry, not a billing ledger. Transport failures and in-flight responses can also separate the client and server counts.

panels.title: Stock / client responses
panels.description: Stock exporter request rate divided by responses received from the stock shop, measured independently in the load generator. Includes 500 responses. Both use a one-hour window. A value near 1x is expected with correct counting. Warm-up, in-flight responses and transport failures affect the comparison.

panels.title: Request rate vs client responses
panels.description: Blue is the merged endpoint. Orange is the stock exporter. Green independently counts responses received from the merged shop, including HTTP 500. Violet markers infer replacement workers from new worker IDs, without identifying the exit signal.

targets.legendFormat: one count for the whole shop

targets.expr: count by (worker) (label_replace((max by (cluster_worker_id) (worker_heap_used{job="shop-api"}) unless max by (cluster_worker_id) (worker_heap_used{job="shop-api"} offset $__interval)) and on () count(max by (cluster_worker_id) (worker_heap_used{job="shop-api"} offset $__interval)), "worker", "$1", "cluster_worker_id", "([0-9]+):.*"))

matcher.options: one count for the whole shop

panels.title: Counter decreases across all series, last hour
panels.description: Counts decreases across route and status series, not worker exits. Switching the worker serving the shared stock port can look like a reset. Merged worker totals are retained, but a primary restart resets those totals too.

targets.legendFormat: one count for the whole shop

matcher.options: one count for the whole shop

panels.title: Workers the graph can see (the shop runs four)
panels.description: Both shops run four workers. The merged endpoint reports all live worker gauges. The stock exporter reports only the worker answering that scrape. Replacement startup can briefly reduce the live count.

targets.legendFormat: one count for the whole shop

matcher.options: one count for the whole shop

panels.title: Merged / client responses
panels.description: Merged request rate divided by HTTP responses received from the merged shop, independently counted by the load generator. Includes 500 responses. SIGKILL may lose recent metrics, and transport failures can also separate these counts. This is a comparison, not a lossless guarantee.

panels.title: The raw counter, and what each setup has counted
Requests counter as Prometheus sees it
panels.description: The raw running count. The merged endpoint retains worker totals. The stock endpoint shows one worker per scrape, so switching workers can make the count jump or drop. Violet markers infer new worker IDs from successive samples.

panels.title: Requests counted, whole shop
panels.description: Latest retained worker snapshots since the primary started. A graceful final preserves the leaving worker totals. A hard kill can lose increments recorded after its last snapshot.

panels.title: Requests counted, usual setup (one worker only)
panels.description: Not the shop's total: only the count kept by whichever worker answered the last scrape. Right after that worker is swapped it reads as low as 1.

panels.title: p95 request latency
panels.description: Merged histograms add counts, sums and buckets across workers. The usual setup's line is one worker's sample.

panels.title: Requests per second by route
panels.description: Monotonic sums: one latest snapshot per worker, retired workers' totals kept.

panels.title: Checkout errors per minute
panels.description: About 3% of checkouts fail on purpose.

panels.title: In-flight requests and email queue, whole cluster
panels.description: Non-monotonic sums add current worker values and drop exited workers. Each checkout queues confirmation emails, and the queue gauge is summed across live workers.

panels.description: Heap gauges use a separate series for each worker and boot. A line ends when its worker is retired and a new one starts with the next ID.

panels.description: The handler returns 503 for an incomplete round instead of partial data.

Client transport failures, last hour
panels.description: Failed or timed-out requests per target. HTTP 500 responses count as received responses and are not transport failures. A mismatch between server and client counters is not solely evidence of telemetry loss.

options.content:
**shop-api** uses [otel-cluster-metrics](https://github.com/adityareddy-dev/otel-cluster-metrics). **shop-api-stock** runs a stock OpenTelemetry Prometheus exporter in each worker on one shared port. The independent **load** process counts attempts, received responses, transport failures and in-flight requests for each target at `/metrics`.

Prometheus scrapes all three every 15 seconds. The default demo replaces the oldest worker every four minutes, choosing SIGKILL with 20% probability and SIGTERM otherwise. Violet bars show new worker IDs, not exit signals. The primary logs each actual exit signal. A hard kill can lose the last worker snapshot window, normally up to 10 seconds. A primary restart loses the retained aggregate.

Run [examples/grafana](https://github.com/adityareddy-dev/otel-cluster-metrics/tree/main/examples/grafana) with `docker compose up`, then open Grafana on port 3000. Wait at least two scrapes for rates. The shape changes as workers age and restart. No fixed inflation factor is promised. For known-input correctness, run `npm test` and `node examples/single-task-workers.cjs` from the repository root.
